editorial:
Picture a giant old mansion, a dead mystery writer, and a family full of greedy relatives who all want his money. That is the world you step into with Knives Out. Detective Benoit Blanc, played with charm and a thick Southern accent, arrives to figure out who killed Harlan Thrombey. Every family member has a secret, and every conversation feels like a trap. The movie mixes sharp humor with a classic whodunit feel, so you are laughing one minute and guessing the next.

The acting is fantastic across the board, especially Daniel Craig as Blanc and Ana de Armas as Marta, the kind nurse who becomes the heart of the story. The pacing stays quick, the clues are clever, and the twists keep you on your toes. On the downside, some jokes land better than others, and a few side characters feel underused. Still, if you enjoy smart mysteries with a fun tone, this is a great pick.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, you learn that Marta accidentally gave Harlan the wrong medication, but Harlan actually switched the labels to protect her. He then killed himself to make it look like suicide. Blanc reveals that Ransom, Harlan's grandson, swapped the drugs to frame Marta. Ransom is arrested, and Marta inherits the entire estate, standing on the balcony as the family looks up at her in shock.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves clever whodunits and sharp comedy.
